Cartoonists Combine is a collective that has spent over four decades bringing together artists and represents more than 100 cartoonists in Maharashtra. It was founded in 1983 on the initiative of Balasaheb Thackeray, himself a political cartoonist. But at 2 am on November 20, Instagram temporarily restricted the collective’s account in India. Gaurav Sarjerao, president of the collective, said an Instagram notification on November 19 – restricting access to a post in India – had warned that the account could be restricted “if you continue to share such content”. That post had contained a cartoon depicting PM Modi as a king whose life depended on a parrot, with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar portrayed as the parrot. “I am not sure whether the account was taken down because of that particular cartoon, but we did receive a notification regarding it,” said Sarjerao. items.summary: A new Supreme Court bench on Monday reduced the scope of the case on unauthorised construction and residential land misuse across India [ Loganathan vs. State of Tamil Nadu & Ors. ]. The case was recently reassigned to the present bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Sanjeev Sachdeva from a bench led by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah. The bench of Justice Amanullah had taken up the exercise of violations of building laws across India despite the individual case before it having been disposed off. This had led to a spate of new petitions and applications before the Court. When the matter came up before the bench of Justices Nagarathna and Sachdeva today, the Court observed that a dismissed appeal cannot be turned into an open-ended forum for settling disputes across the country. Accordingly, the bench disposed of all pending intervention and individual applications, granting liberty to affected parties to approach local municipal authorities, statutory tribunals, or their respective High Courts. items.title: Mumbai court grants anticipatory bail to Muslim man in city's first anti-conversion law case
items.summary: A Mumbai sessions court on November 20 granted anticipatory bail to a Muslim man booked under the newly enacted Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act, 2026, for allegedly forcing his Hindu wife to convert to Islam. This case marks the first arrest in Mumbai and possibly the first anticipatory bail application across Maharashtra under the anti-conversion law. Additional Sessions Judge PA Sane of the City Civil and Sessions Court at Dindoshi in Mumbai passed the order after the Hindu woman's mother lodged a complaint alleging unlawful religious conversion. During the hearing, the complainant and prosecution relied on a wedding invitation card pairing a Muslim name with the Hindu woman's identity, alongside a photograph showing her in a burkha. The court noted that the couple had already registered a civil marriage under the Special Marriage Act on October 16 following prior statutory notice. Further, a register seized by police from a Maulavi contained no entry confirming that a religious Nikah ceremony had taken place. items.summary: National interest and the country's economy takes precedence, a special court in Mumbai said on Friday (November 20) while rejecting a plea by convicted stockbroker Ketan Parekh seeking permission to travel abroad for 91 days [Ketan Parekh v. SEBI]. The special SEBI court observed that allowing a three-month long travel approval for overseas trip would enable Parekh, who was behind the 2000-2001 securities scam, to engage in further violations of securities laws. “It would not be expedient in the national interest and economy of the country to permit the applicant/accused to travel abroad for a longer period of three months. The possibility of applicant/accused indulging such unlawful activity in contravention to the securities law can not be ruled out if such, blanket permission for a period of three months is granted to the applicant/accused,” SEBI special judge RM Jadhav observed. Parekh approached the court seeking permission to visit Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the UAE, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark and Switzerland for a family vacation without furnishing any additional security deposit. items.title: Technology can undermine justice if poorly designed: Delhi High Court Justice Tejas Karia
items.summary: Technology, if poorly designed, can cause more harm than good in India's justice system, said Delhi High Court judge Justice Tejas Karia on Sunday. Justice Karia was speaking at the inaugural edition of JusTech, a national conclave organised by the Dharmashastra National Law University. Jabalpur (DNLU). His address focused on addressing the justice gap by harnessing technology. He pointed out that the justice gap does not arise because of any lacunae in law, but due to various barriers such as cost, accessibility, complexity, undue delays, and a lack of trust in the system. Justice Karia opined that Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) can be a handy tool to bridge the gap, without replacing human involvement. " Mediation is the norm of the day. We all know that mediation is very valuable, but if it can be done in online mode, what all it can achieve: all the barriers which we just discussed can be easily eliminated with the help of an Online Dispute Resolution mechanism. items.title: US court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 19 years in jail for plot to kill Gurpatwant Pannun
items.summary: A United States Court on Friday sentenced Indian National Nikhil Gupta to 19 years and 7 months in jail for his involvement in a plot to assassinate Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in America. Judge Victor Marrero of the Southern District of New York passed the order. Nikhil Gupta is accused of orchestrating a contract killing of US-based Sikh separatist leader and lawyer Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York in 2023. According to the US Department of Justice (DOJ), Gupta was recruited in May 2023 by Vikash Yadav, an Indian government employee who allegedly worked with him to arrange Pannun's assassination. Prosecutors alleged that Gupta approached a criminal associate for help in hiring a contract killer. However, the associate was actually a confidential source working with the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), who introduced Gupta to an undercover DEA officer posing as a hitman. The indictment alleged that Yadav agreed to pay $100,000 for the killing and that an associate delivered an advance payment of $15,000 on June 9, 2023. items.title: South Central 102: How Deutsche Bank enabled money laundering and sanctioned oligarchs
items.summary: Can a global banking giant like Deutsche Bank be held accountable for allegedly enabling money laundering and hiding sanctioned oligarchs? What do 15.5 million leaked Deutsche Bank documents reveal about the bank’s role in the global financial system? In this week’s South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna examine a major international investigation into Deutsche Bank. They are joined by investigative journalist Josy Joseph, who led the investigation against Deutsche Bank. The investigation is based on approximately 15.5 million internal documents. Josy explains how the documents point to Deutsche Bank’s role in enabling sanctioned oligarchs to conceal their wealth and facilitating large-scale money laundering. He describes the bank as one of the central pieces of infrastructure in the global financial system, with its operations and correspondent banking networks spanning countries across the world. items.title: Women in high public office does not mean equality has been achieved: Justice BV Nagarathna at Oxford
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice BV Nagarathna recently said that the presence of women in high public offices does not mean equality has been achieved across the society. She added that even a guaranteed right can be difficult to exercise in practice due to cost, delay and social consequences. "The existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society. A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies," the judge said. The judge made the comment while delivering the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at the Oxford India Centre for Sustainable Development in Somerville College, University of Oxford, on November 18. The lecture was on the topic "The Doors She Opened: Cornelia Sorabji and the Progress of Women's Rights in India." Such an interpretation would defeat the object of prescribing a definite period for completion of reassessment proceedings, " the verdict said. Hence, it set aside the tax additions.
